definition: Training agents against copies or past versions of themselves so the opponent curriculum scales automatically (AlphaZero, and AlphaStar's league of diverse exploiter agents).
details: Training agents against copies or past versions of themselves so the opponent curriculum scales automatically (AlphaZero, and AlphaStar's league of diverse exploiter agents). The game-theoretic counterpart of LLM self-improvement (see Self-Improvement), now resurfacing in automated red teaming and negotiation agents.

explainer.lead: Self-play and league training train agents against copies or past versions of themselves, so the opponent curriculum scales automatically. It matters because it is the game-theoretic counterpart of LLM self-improvement, now resurfacing in automated red teaming and negotiation agents.

tiers.eli5: You get better at a game by playing against earlier versions of yourself, and against a whole roster of rivals, so the challenge keeps growing.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers train agents against copies or past versions, as in AlphaZero, and use AlphaStar's league of diverse exploiter agents. A pitfall is that the curriculum scales automatically, so opponents must be chosen to keep the challenge meaningful.
tiers.paperLevel: Formally, agents are trained against copies or past versions of themselves so the opponent curriculum scales automatically. Known instantiations are AlphaZero and AlphaStar's league of diverse exploiter agents.

explainer.example: An agent plays against its own past checkpoints, and a league adds diverse exploiter agents that target its weaknesses, keeping training opponents challenging.
